title: Add benchmark-lab multi-variant reporting and profiling pipeline v65
author: Sophie Chen
description:
Motivation: extend the benchmark-lab reporting pipeline to support multi-variant profiling runs and consolidated summaries for per-variant baselines. This PR adds end-to-end reporting for multi-variant experiments (model + quantization + batch profile variants), improves the profiling baseline ingestion logic, and introduces a light-weight renderer for trend dashboards.

What this PR does: - Adds multi-variant job runner that schedules variant permutations and stores per-variant metadata. - Adds variant-aware aggregation steps in the reporting pipeline (raw -> normalized -> per-variant baseline). - Introduces a compact JSON schema for variant metadata to keep storage costs down. - Implements additional CI perf checks that compare new baselines to last-stable baselines and surface regressions as warnings. - Adds an ops playbook for triggering rebaseline runs and for interpreting multi-variant dashboards.

Checklist: - [x] Add multi-variant runners and job definitions - [x] Update reporting pipeline transforms and aggregation - [x] Add variant metadata schema + migration script - [x] Add CI perf check and local runner integration test - [x] Update docs and ops playbook - [x] Add unit + integration tests

Notes: The description includes background on why multi-variant is important: prior pipeline assumed a single "profile key" per experiment which made it hard to reason about combined changes across quantization and batching settings. This work enables us to compare like-for-like across variants and to produce per-variant SLAs.

Related: follows on work in pr-223456 and pr-231234 which introduced the initial multi-variant experiment proto and pulled partial aggregation. Linear tasks ENG-4211/ENG-4302 track rollout and validation. SUP-88 surfaced the need for stable baselines after a customer incident where a quantized model exhibited throughput regression.

Migration / rollout plan: This is backwards compatible for existing single-variant runs. A migration script (scripts/migrate/upgrade-variant-metadata.py) coalesces legacy profile keys into a single-variant variant metadata object. Feature rollout is gated behind a feature flag `benchmark.multi_variant_v65` and will be toggled after a canary run that executes 50 representative workloads.

Risks: The main risk is increased storage footprint for per-variant metrics; mitigations include compacting the metric payload and retention policies. CI perf checks are conservative and run as warnings on first deployment; they will be tightened after two stable runs.

chore(bench): variant metadata schema and migration script

ci: add perf regression checker and e2e job

file_snippets: benchmark-lab/runners/multi_variant_runner.py: added schedule_variant_job(job_spec) that enumerates model x quant x batch configs and writes job metadata to jobs/
benchmark-lab/reporting/aggregators/variant_aggregator.py: new aggregate_per_variant(raw_rows) => normalizes, groups by variant_id, emits per-variant baselines
benchmark-lab/schemas/variant_metadata_v2.json: compact schema with fields [variant_id, tags, config_hash, seed, parent_run_id]
benchmark-lab/scripts/migrate/upgrade-variant-metadata.py: script coalesces legacy profile_key into variant_metadata_v2, idempotent with dry-run flag
review_conversation: Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Can we avoid storing full config blobs for each variant? Storing hashes + referenced config reduces storage — consider moving large params to blobstore.

Sophie Chen (author): Good point — migration script stores a config_hash and we push full configs to s3://benchmark-configs/ with lifecycle rules. Updated migration script to include `--push-configs` flag.
Arjun Nair (reviewer): CI perf check looks good but it currently uses a 2% threshold which might be noisy for small models. Suggest making thresholds model-class aware.
Sophie Chen (author): Made threshold configurable per-model-class and added conservative defaults. Added unit test coverage for threshold selection.
Priya Kapoor (reviewer): Please add a short runbook section for when rebaseline is required after infra change (driver/kernel updates).
Sophie Chen (author): Added ops playbook section and a script `scripts/rebaseline/trigger_rebaseline.sh` to automate staged rebaseline runs.
Liam O'Connor (approver): Verified canary run results and storage estimates. Approving.
testing_notes: Added an integration e2e that runs a small multi-variant job against a local emulator. Canary run executed on staging against 50 representative workloads; no regressions beyond expected variance. Local devs can run `make bench-e2e` to reproduce with reduced workload set.
ops_playbook_summary: Contains steps for: 1) running canary multi-variant experiments; 2) interpreting per-variant baselines on the dashboard; 3) triggering automated rebaseline; 4) rollback steps if a variant shows regression beyond threshold.
release_notes: Added multi-variant reporting and profiling pipeline (v65). This enables per-variant baselines for combined model/quant/batch experiments, variant-aware aggregation, and a CI perf check that surfaces baseline regressions. Backwards compatible for existing runs. Feature gated behind `benchmark.multi_variant_v65`.
post_merge_tasks: 1) Flip feature flag for internal staging canary. 2) Schedule a 2-week retention review for variant metrics. 3) Monitor perf-check warnings in the next 3 runs and tighten thresholds if stable.
